def render_g_revenue_by_region(pdf, dataframes, x, y, w, h):
    # Access primary dataset
    df = dataframes.get('sales_pipeline.csv')
    if df is None or df.empty:
        # Fallback: if no data, write a placeholder
        pdf.set_xy(x, y)
        pdf.set_font("Helvetica", "B", 10)
        pdf.cell(w, h, "Sem dados de receita por região", border=0, align='C')
        return

    # Aggregate total revenue by region
    rev_agg = df.groupby('region', as_index=False)['revenue'].sum()
    rev_agg = rev_agg.sort_values('revenue', ascending=False)  # highest first

    # Prepare data for chart
    regions = rev_agg['region'].tolist()
    revenues = rev_agg['revenue'].tolist()

    # Optionally include targets from second file
    df_targets = dataframes.get('regional_targets.xlsx')
    if df_targets is not None and not df_targets.empty:
        # Map target values per region
        target_dict = dict(zip(df_targets['region'], df_targets['quarterly_target']))
        targets = [target_dict.get(r, 0) for r in regions]
    else:
        targets = None

    # Import required modules (assumed already imported globally)
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    import tempfile
    import os

    # Create figure with proper dimensions (mm -> inches)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(w / 25.4, h / 25.4))

    # Plot bars
    bar_colors = ['#4C72B0', '#55A868', '#C44E52']  # safe colorblind-friendly palette
    bars = ax.bar(regions, revenues, color=bar_colors[:len(regions)], edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5)

    # Add target markers if available
    if targets:
        for i, (r, rev, target) in enumerate(zip(regions, revenues, targets)):
            if target > 0:
                # Plot a horizontal dashed line all the way? Better: point marker above bar?
                # We'll draw a small horizontal line segment on top of the bar (or at the target value)
                ax.hlines(y=target, xmin=i-0.25, xmax=i+0.25, colors='#333333', linewidth=1.5, linestyles='dashed')
                # Add a small label at the end
                ax.text(i+0.3, target, f'Meta: R$ {target:,.0f}', fontsize=6, va='bottom', ha='left', color='#333333')
        # Also add a legend item for target line
        ax.plot([], [], color='#333333', linestyle='dashed', linewidth=1.5, label='Meta trimestral')
        ax.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=6, frameon=False)

    # Annotate bar values (only if height is sufficient)
    if h / 25.4 > 1.5:  # roughly > 38 mm
        for i, (bar, rev) in enumerate(zip(bars, revenues)):
            ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, bar.get_height() + 0.02 * max(revenues),
                    f'R$ {rev/1000:.1f}k', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=7, fontweight='normal')

    # Title and labels in Portuguese
    ax.set_title('Receita Total por Região', fontsize=9, pad=8, fontweight='bold')
    ax.set_xlabel('Região', fontsize=7)
    ax.set_ylabel('Receita (R$)', fontsize=7)

    # Format y-axis with plain style
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda x, _: f'R$ {x:,.0f}'))
    ax.tick_params(axis='both', labelsize=6)

    # Remove top/right spines
    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

    # Adjust layout to prevent clipping (especially if legend is present)
    fig.subplots_adjust(top=0.82, bottom=0.20, left=0.18, right=0.95)

    # Save to temporary PNG with high DPI
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".png", delete=False) as tmp:
        plt.savefig(tmp.name, dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight', pad_inches=0.05)
        plt.close()
        pdf.image(tmp.name, x=x, y=y, w=w, h=h)

def render_g_revenue_by_product(pdf, dataframes, x, y, w, h):
    """
    Renders a bar chart of total revenue per product (Alpha, Beta, Gamma).
    Highlights the top product and includes a dynamic title.
    """
    df = dataframes.get("sales_pipeline.csv")
    
    # Handle missing/invalid data gracefully
    if df is None or df.empty:
        # Create a placeholder image
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
        import tempfile
        import os
        
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(w/25.4, h/25.4))
        ax.text(0.5, 0.5, "Dados indisponíveis", ha='center', va='center',
                fontsize=14, transform=ax.transAxes)
        ax.axis('off')
        
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".png", delete=False) as tmp:
            plt.savefig(tmp.name, dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight', pad_inches=0.05)
            plt.close()
            pdf.image(tmp.name, x=x, y=y, w=w, h=h)
            os.unlink(tmp.name)
        return
    
    # Aggregate revenue by product
    revenue_by_product = df.groupby("product")["revenue"].sum().reset_index()
    products = revenue_by_product["product"].tolist()
    revenues = revenue_by_product["revenue"].tolist()
    
    # Identify top product
    max_rev = max(revenues)
    top_product = revenue_by_product.loc[revenue_by_product["revenue"].idxmax(), "product"]
    top_rev_formatted = f"{max_rev:,.0f}".replace(",", ".")
    
    # Create figure with exact dimensions
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(w/25.4, h/25.4))
    fig.subplots_adjust(top=0.85, bottom=0.20)  # reserve space for title and labels
    
    # Generate bar colors: highlight top product
    colors = ["#2c7bb6" if rev != max_rev else "#d7191c" for rev in revenues]
    bars = ax.bar(products, revenues, color=colors, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.8)
    
    # Add value labels on bars if height is sufficient (h >= 70mm)
    if h >= 70:
        max_y = max(revenues) * 1.15
        ax.set_ylim(0, max_y)
        for bar, rev in zip(bars, revenues):
            ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., bar.get_height() + max_y*0.02,
                    f"R${rev:,.0f}".replace(",", "."), ha='center', va='bottom',
                    fontsize=8, fontweight='bold')
    else:
        # No space for labels, just ensure enough headroom for bars
        ax.set_ylim(0, max(revenues) * 1.10)
    
    # Format y-axis with thousands separator (Brazilian style)
    from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter
    def brazilian_formatter(x, pos):
        return f"R${x:,.0f}".replace(",", ".")
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(brazilian_formatter))
    
    # Labels and title
    ax.set_xlabel("Produto", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_ylabel("Receita (R$)", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_title(f"Receita por Produto\n{top_product} lidera com R$ {top_rev_formatted}",
                 fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
    
    # Remove top/right spines
    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
    
    # Adjust tick font size
    ax.tick_params(axis='both', labelsize=8)
    
    # Save and insert into PDF
    import tempfile
    import os
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".png", delete=False) as tmp:
        plt.savefig(tmp.name, dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight', pad_inches=0.05)
        plt.close()
        pdf.image(tmp.name, x=x, y=y, w=w, h=h)
        os.unlink(tmp.name)

import os
os.environ.setdefault('MPLCONFIGDIR', '/tmp/matplotlib')
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from fpdf import FPDF, XPos, YPos
import tempfile
import textwrap

sns.set_theme(style='whitegrid')

def _safe_pdf_text(value):
    replacements = {
        '\u2013': '-', '\u2014': '-', '\u2015': '-',
        '\u2018': "'", '\u2019': "'", '\u201c': '"', '\u201d': '"',
        '\u2022': '-', '\u00a0': ' ', '\u2026': '...'
    }
    text = str(value or '')
    for source, target in replacements.items():
        text = text.replace(source, target)
    return text.encode('latin-1', 'replace').decode('latin-1')

def _wrap_lines(text, max_chars):
    lines = []
    for paragraph in str(text).splitlines() or ['']:
        wrapped = textwrap.wrap(paragraph.strip(), width=max_chars) or ['']
        lines.extend(wrapped)
    return lines

def _sentence_chunks(text):
    normalized = ' '.join(str(text).split())
    chunks, current = [], []
    for token in normalized.split(' '):
        current.append(token)
        if token.rstrip().endswith(('.', '!', '?', ';')):
            chunks.append(' '.join(current))
            current = []
    if current:
        chunks.append(' '.join(current))
    return chunks or [normalized]

def _fit_text_to_box(text, w, h, font_size, line_height):
    max_chars = max(14, int(w * 0.55 * (10 / max(font_size, 1))))
    max_lines = max(1, int(h / max(line_height, 1)))
    if len(_wrap_lines(text, max_chars)) <= max_lines:
        return text
    selected = []
    for sentence in _sentence_chunks(text):
        candidate = ' '.join(selected + [sentence]).strip()
        if not candidate:
            continue
        if len(_wrap_lines(candidate, max_chars)) <= max_lines:
            selected.append(sentence)
        elif selected:
            break
        else:
            words = sentence.split()
            compact = []
            for word in words:
                candidate = ' '.join(compact + [word])
                if len(_wrap_lines(candidate, max_chars)) > max_lines:
                    break
                compact.append(word)
            selected.append(' '.join(compact))
            break
    fitted = ' '.join(selected).strip()
    return fitted

def _write_report_title(pdf, title, font_family):
    clean_title = ' '.join(_safe_pdf_text(title or 'Relatório Analítico').split())
    for size in range(16, 10, -1):
        max_chars = max(28, int(58 * (16 / size)))
        lines = textwrap.wrap(clean_title, width=max_chars) or [clean_title]
        if len(lines) <= 2:
            pdf.set_font(font_family, 'B', size)
            pdf.multi_cell(0, 8, '\n'.join(lines), new_x=XPos.LMARGIN, new_y=YPos.NEXT, align='C')
            return
    pdf.set_font(font_family, 'B', 11)
    pdf.multi_cell(0, 7, '\n'.join(textwrap.wrap(clean_title, width=84)), new_x=XPos.LMARGIN, new_y=YPos.NEXT, align='C')

def render_text_block(pdf, text, x, y, w, h, title=None):
    font_size = 10
    line_height = 5
    text = _safe_pdf_text(text)
    title = _safe_pdf_text(title) if title else None
    body_height = h
    pdf.set_xy(x, y)
    if title:
        pdf.set_font('helvetica', 'B', font_size)
        pdf.cell(w, 7, title, new_x=XPos.LMARGIN, new_y=YPos.NEXT)
        body_height = max(1, h - 8)
        pdf.set_xy(x, pdf.get_y())
    
    fitted_text = _fit_text_to_box(text, w, body_height, font_size, line_height)
    pdf.set_font('helvetica', '', font_size)
    pdf.multi_cell(w, line_height, fitted_text, align='J')

                    fontsize=8, fontweight='bold')
    else:
        # No space for labels, just ensure enough headroom for bars
        ax.set_ylim(0, max(revenues) * 1.10)
    
    # Format y-axis with thousands separator (Brazilian style)
    from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter
    def brazilian_formatter(x, pos):
        return f"R${x:,.0f}".replace(",", ".")
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(brazilian_formatter))
    
    # Labels and title
    ax.set_xlabel("Produto", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_ylabel("Receita (R$)", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_title(f"Receita por Produto\n{top_product} lidera com R$ {top_rev_formatted}",
                 fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
    
    # Remove top/right spines
    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
    
    # Adjust tick font size
    ax.tick_params(axis='both', labelsize=8)
    
    # Save and insert into PDF
    import tempfile
    import os
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".png", delete=False) as tmp:
        plt.savefig(tmp.name, dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight', pad_inches=0.05)
        plt.close()
        pdf.image(tmp.name, x=x, y=y, w=w, h=h)
        os.unlink(tmp.name)
